pattern.crimePattern: a committee secretary bribed to forge a community-land vote poisons the elder who found the torn-out page, then guides the detective through the case
pattern.notes: Fictional committee, company (Waso Range Investments) and people. The land conflict is inside one community and one company, never between communities (region rule). The poison is named only as cattle-dip concentrate; no dose or method of mixing is given. Spine background: Till 880 214 and a file "withdrawn — J.E.".

ob.reportedBy: Family of the deceased, Garba Tula
ob.text: A family reports an elder, Boru Tadicha (66), chairman of the Garba Tula community land management committee, found dead in his bed at 04:30. Suspected heart failure. The family asks for a police look because "he had enemies over the land".

reconstruction.text: April. The community assembly rejects the lease, 212 to 41. Dabaso, as secretary, records it on page 11.

May. Waso Range pays him KSh 3 million through Till 880 214. He tears out page 11, types "minutes" approving the lease, stamps them with the committee's retired stamp and files them. Three weeks later the county's copy of the registration file is "withdrawn — J.E.".
Tuesday. Boru opens the book to prepare Saturday's assembly and finds page 11 gone. He tells Dabaso, his oldest ally, that the book is going to the assembly and the police.
Thursday, 20:00. Dabaso brings camel-milk tea in his red flask, mixed with dip concentrate from the committee store. Boru drinks two cups. Dabaso leaves at 21:00 with the flask.
Boru is sick by eleven and dead by four. On Friday morning Dabaso is the first relative at the house, and offers to translate.

afterVerdict.beat: Pattern File, t_mvua: KSh 3 million from Till 880 214. t_registry: the Garba Tula file "withdrawn — Registry, Nairobi — J.E.". Amani's notebook: "Withdrawn. Like Dad's field book in Nakuru. Same word."

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Dabaso and a warrant on his home. Detain him after the search; toxicology takes 18 h plus 4 h transport and lands at detention hour 23, the tightest in the region. The post-mortem at Isiolo runs in parallel.

ui.beatNotes: The ally's translations. For the first half of the case Dabaso's translations appear in the notebook in his handwriting. They are accurate, but one thing is missing: "he brought the tea in his red flask" becomes "we had tea". The full sentence appears when Halake re-interviews Mama Darmi in Borana. The notebook shows the two side by side. Translations are evidence too.
